claims.text:
stage computation: Two repeatable actions Progress and TV. Progress outcome0 deterministic, initial predictor1, then predictor updates exactly to0 after observation; squared intrinsic error1 then0. TV outcome independent Bernoulli(.5), optimal predictor.5, expected squared error .5*(0−.5)²+.5*(1−.5)²=.25 each visit. Intrinsic-only expected-error chooser picks Progress initially1>.25, then TV.25>0. Separate extrinsic rewards Progress1/TV0 are not used by that chooser.

**Countercase / boundary:** Use combined score extrinsic+.1*expected intrinsic: after learning Progress score1 versusTV.025, so chooses Progress. Change TV to deterministic1 with predictor learned after one observation: residual error0, so persistent .25 disappears. Prediction error does not necessarily mean learnable progress. These are declared expected scores, not motivations or measured behaviour of real agents.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict where intrinsic-only choice goes after Progress is learned; recall a perfectly learned deterministicTV has no residual surprise, whereas randomTV remains noisy even for an optimal mean predictor.

**Intervention / reachable witness:** Observe Progress updates its predictor; Intrinsic/Combined and Deterministic TV recompute choice and expected error terms, retaining both initial and post-learning decisions. Mark expected TV error distinctly from one realized sample. No claim to simulate curiosity as human feeling.
